source: Tableau Cloud published datasource 'v.HfdV3', Contracts table, joined to the 167 providers this team sourced
system: Tableau Cloud VizQL Data Service (https://10az.online.tableau.com, site healthcarefinancedirect, datasource LUID 583b19c2-c2ac-4aa4-a207-4714da9a0262). Moved off direct SQL on 2026-09-20 because a scheduled cloud session has no VPN and cannot reach Analytics.dw.FactContract.

tableauQuery.cohortFilter: Provider Unique Key is one of the 167 ids in data/sourced_pids.txt
tableauQuery.grain: TRUNC_DAY(Contract Created), one result set re-aggregated into every period below
tableauQuery.fanoutGuard: COUNT(Contract Id) is compared to COUNTD(Contract Unique Key) on every day; the run aborts if they diverge, which is how a relationship fan-out in a multi-fact datasource would present

joinKey: Provider Unique Key = the HubSpot COMPANY.provider_unique_key of each sourced company. The cohort is filtered on the Providers-table field Provider Unique Key, not on Contract Provider Key, because the contract-side field only contains providers that have originated and a SET filter on it rejects the whole query when a sourced provider has produced nothing yet.
cohortFile: data/sourced_pids.txt, regenerated by build.py from the current sourced flag - never a hand-typed list

validation.method: Tableau VDS figure compared to the identical query against Analytics.dw.FactContract over the local SQL connection
validation.result: exact agreement on all five periods and on lifetime

caveats: Cancellations restate this DOWNWARD after the fact. Re-running the identical query on the identical window days later returns less, because contracts inside the window have since been cancelled. A figure quoted from a screenshot will not reconcile later, and that is the data behaving correctly, not an error. Always read these as as-of the run date.

Read through Tableau Cloud, not the SQL warehouse. On 2026-09-20 the two were compared on the identical cohort and windows and agreed to the cent and to the contract on all five periods and on lifetime. The Tableau side is the Contracts logical table of v.HfdV3, which is one row per contract, and the run aborts if a day's contract count ever stops matching its distinct-contract-key count.

v.HfdV3 is a rolling extract. The earliest contract in this cohort is 2025-09-18, so nothing in these figures is clipped by that window today - but a cohort with older history would show a lifetime figure that is short by whatever falls off the back of the extract.
Only 59 of the 167 sourced practices have originated anything at all.
The cohort moves as the 90-day window rolls, so month values shift between refreshes for two reasons at once: different days AND a different set of practices. Compare cohorts, not just months.

All five periods are cut from ONE day-grain result set, so they are mutually consistent by construction. producingProviders is a DISTINCT count WITHIN each period and therefore does NOT add up across periods: a practice that produced in both weeks is counted in both.
This is originated treatment volume, not HFD revenue. Cash actually released to providers runs about 82% of it.
Not computable in HubSpot: every money property there is a lifetime total or a fixed calendar snapshot with no date dimension.
The join rests on the contact-to-company link, which is the weakest joint in the build.
